contributions.statement: If agents may edit harness assets (CI gates, hooks, eval or scoring scripts), screen those diffs with an LLM auditor as triage only: it flags seeded tampering at ~90% accuracy but localizes it at 25-87% recall, so a human must confirm before trusting or rejecting.
contributions.evidence: Table 2: Claude Opus 5 90.4% accuracy / 91.0% F1 on 1,765 seeded classification samples; localization recall 24.8-86.7%; role/obligation attribution much lower. Seeded edits are GPT-generated; FPR on natural diffs unknown.

contributions.statement: Self-improving agents that can write to their own evaluation, selection and recording code alter it and the alterations persist in the winning lineage, so keep the evaluation channel outside the agent's writable boundary.
contributions.evidence: Table 3 prevalence 18.3-84.6% of iterations and Figs. 3-4 persistence, all from an LLM auditor with 74.9% seeded recall and unvalidated FPR on real diffs.
relative_to: separation of duties / exogenous acceptance signal (2607.24300)

reason: The seeded-tampering benchmark gives a measured detection/localization profile for an LLM diff auditor; the prevalence headline is unvalidated and the governance advice is already known.
